text: Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League clash between Nottingham Forest and Luton Town.
We are set for a big game at the City Ground between two sides in the bottom seven of the Premier League table.
Forest, who are 13th, could climb into the top half with a victory here.
Meanwhile, 17th-place Luton could pull clear of the relegation zone should they take the spoils.
Steve Cooper makes a single change from Forest's goalless draw at Crystal Palace last time out.
It comes on the left wing with Elanga replacing Callum Hudson-Odoi.
Niakhite returns from a ban on the bench, but Taiwo Awoniyi, Gonzalo Montiel, Danilo, Felipe, Nuno Tavares and Wayne Hennessey form a lengthy injury list.
As for Luton, Rob Edwards makes two alterations to the side that began the defeat against Tottenham before the international break.
Mengi replaces Mads Andersen, who faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines with a hamstring injury, while Brown takes Abebayo's place up front.
Dan Potts, Amari'i Bell, Jordan Clark and Albert Sambi Lokonga are unavailable for the Hatters through injury.
Forest have lost just two of their last 18 Premier League games on home soil.
That will stand them in good stead against Luton, who have won on just one of their last 14 visits to the City Ground.
The teams are out and we are almost ready to go.
Referee Samuel Barrott blows his whistle and Luton get the match under way!
Wood looks to cushion the ball into Elanga's path on the edge of the penalty area.
But Luton have plenty of players back to snuff out the danger.
Forest are aiming to end a four-game winless streak today.
The Reds have drawn three times during that run.
CHANCE! Good link-up play releases Toffolo down the left flank.
The full-back's cross finds Wood, whose volley is held by Kaminski
The hosts continue to threaten and Sangare heads Aurier's cross towards goal, but it is just too high.
INCHES AWAY! Luton respond and Ogbene whips a delicious ball across the face of goal.
Morris and Brown slide in to connect, but cannot quite do so to apply the finishing touch.
You must go back to 1987 for the last time Luton won successive away games in the top flight.
Can they break that unwanted streak today?
Elanga looks to work his way into the Luton area, but Burke does well to deny him before Sangare is penalised for bundling over Lockyer.
Forest change the angle from a corner, which Gibbs-White plays short before eventually whipping the ball into the box.
But Kaminski is equal to it.
Not quite! On the turn, Brown looks to guide a low cross towards goal, but drags the ball wide of the far post.
Luton are still finding their feet in the Premier League, having lost six of their opening eight games.
But a couple of positive results would help build momentum and potentially keep them away from trouble.
Premier League winner Wes Morgan is watching on from the stands.
The former defender, who captained Leicester City to top-flight glory in 2015-16, previously made over 400 appearances for Forest.
Forest have enjoyed over 60 per cent of the possession, but the game remains goalless at the midway point in the first half.
CLOSE! A let-off for Luton, who fail to clear the ball from inside their six-yard box.
It drops for Toffolo, but Kaminski manages to keep it out and the visitors escape.
Aurier climbs to meet Gibbs-White's corner into the box, but the defender cannot keep his header down.
Forest are five points better off than they were at this stage last season.
Cooper will be hoping his side can stay well clear of danger this time around.
The hosts are awarded a free-kick inside the Luton half after Lockyer fouls Dominguez.
This is a good opportunity to threaten.
Nothing comes of the free-kick as Luton stay alert and are able to clear their lines.
There is a break in play as Chong goes down after he is accidentally caught by Aurier.
The latter's reaction demonstrates the fact it was not intended.
Chong is not moving particularly easily as he gets to his feet and heads towards the touchline.
But he should be fine to continue.
Back in the thick of the action, the ball drops to Chong outside the Forest area.
The winger chests down a clearance and hits a sweet volley, but it is straight into the arms of Turner.
The match is still goalless as we approach the final five minutes of the first half.
Can either side find the breakthrough?
Although Forest have enjoyed 65 per cent of the possession, it is worth noting they are winless in each of their last four league meetings with Luton.
Morris gets his head on the end of Burke's cross from the right.
The striker has plenty of work to do, but sees his looping header only just drop the wrong side of the crossbar.
CHANCE! Wood should score! Following a neat, flowing move by Forest, Aurier slips at a vital moment.
But the defender recovers and chips the ball into the six-yard box, where Wood can only head over the bar.
The striker was under pressure from Ogbene, but still should have done better in all fairness.
WHAT A CHANCE! Sangare must do better! An unmarked Gibbs-White is able to connect with a long ball over the top of the defence.
Kaminski parries his drilled centre into the path of Sangare, but he fires wide from less than 12 yards out.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-0 LUTON TOWN
We are still awaiting the breakthrough at the City Ground, where Nottingham Forest and Luton Town remain in deadlock.
The hosts have seen the better chances go begging - particularly at the end of the half through Chris Wood and Ibrahim Sangare, who were off target from close range.
The two sides registered a combined four shots on target during the opening 45 minutes.
Both must look to be more clinical after the break.
The action resumes at the City Ground.
WOOD!!! 1-0 FOREST! What a start to the second half by the hosts! Forest counter and a neat exchange of passes between Gibbs-White and Elanga releases Wood, who calmly lifts the ball over Kaminski.
Elanga provided a neat throughball for Wood to run onto and finish.
Forest have their tails up and the home fans are right behind their team.
Elanga looks to release Dominguez, but Kaminski races out of goal to clear the danger.
CHANCE! Wood should score! The striker peels away from his marker to meet Gibbs-White's cross to the far post, but cannot keep his header down from close range.
BROWN SHOULD DO BETTER! Luton look to respond at the other end and Ogbene clips the ball towards Brown, but the striker heads straight at Turner with the entire goal to aim at.
Chances are coming for both sides.
Gibbs-White wrestles possession from Mengi and tries his luck from the edge of the box.
Kaminski has to get down and push the ball to safety.
Burke picks up a knock and is unable to continue.
He limps off to be replaced by Kabore.
Luton will hope the decision to substitute Burke was precautionary.
With several players already sidelined, the last thing they will want is another injury.
Both sides have made a purposeful start to the second half and Forest are a goal to the good as we approach the hour mark.
Wood's strike separates the two teams.
Sangare trips Chong and goes into the book.
Good try! Gibbs-White bursts into the area to receive Mangala's pass and cuts onto his left foot, but cannot keep his shot down.
As things stand, Forest would climb into the top half of the Premier League should they hold on for all three points here.
The hosts push for the second goal and the ball drops for Sangare in the box, but he is unable to find the target from close range.
Luton attack at the other end and the ball breaks for Nakamba to strike from distance.
But his long-range attempt is always rising.
Forest threaten from a corner and Dominguez nods the ball towards goal, but Kaminski manages to hold on to his looping header.
Luton make a triple-change.
The first sees Ruddock Mpanzu replaced by Barkley.
Chong also departs the action with Townsend on for his debut.
Adebayo also enters the action in place of Brown.
Adebayo is involved immediately as he connects with Ogbene's drilled centre, but he cannot steer the ball towards goal.
Luton appeal for a penalty as Morris goes down under pressure from Sangare.
However, the referee is not interested.
WOOD AGAIN!!! 2-0 FOREST! It's that man again! Elanga teases Kabore before delivering an inviting cross.
Wood attacks it and brilliantly plants his header just inside the far post, leaving Kaminski clutching at thin air.
Elanga grabs his second assist of the game after providing a lovely cross for Wood to attack.
Forest make three changes.
Kouyate replaces Sangare in the first of those.
Worrall also enters the action with Boly making way.
The third change sees Yates take Dominguez's place.
Yates immediately has an opportunity to make it 3-0, but he fires his shot too high from a tight angle.
Luton make another change with Woodrow replacing Morris up front.
Gibbs-White goes into the book for a needlessly late challenge on Barkley.
OGBENE!!! 2-1! Hope rekindled for Luton! The visitors send in a free-kick from the left that bamboozles the Forest defence and ricochets kindly for Ogbene, who brilliantly fires home on the volley.
There was a lengthy VAR check for a possible offside against Ogbene.
It is tight, but they give the Luton man the benefit of the doubt and the visitors' deficit is halved.
Forest make a double-change.
The first sees Williams replace Elanga.
Aina is also introduced by Cooper with Aurier making way.
There are going to be eight additional minutes played at the end of this game.
Lockyer sent a long ball into the box towards Adebayo, who has brought Luton level in this game.
ADEBAYO!!! 2-2! Luton are level! Adebayo outmuscles Worrall as he controls Lockyer's long ball into the box, before drilling past Turner from eight yards out.
The travelling supporters are ecstatic and rightly so!
What a response by Luton! The visitors seemed well out of this contest at 2-0 down, but it has been a brilliant comeback to bring themselves level.
OFFSIDE, NO GOAL! Wood briefly thinks he has won it for Forest as he latches onto a throughball, and drills it into the bottom corner.

text: But his joy is cut short by the offside flag, and it was the right decision.
We are into the final 60 seconds of stoppage time.
Will this scoreline remain, or are we going to see another dramatic late twist?
Murillo is late on Nakamba and can have no complaints as he goes into the book.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 2-2 LUTON TOWN
Luton produced an inspired late comeback to salvage a point against Forest, who led 2-0 at the City Ground thanks to Wood's brace.
But Ogbene gave the Hatters hope in the 83rd minute, before substitute Adebayo equalised in stoppage time.
The result sees Luton remain 17th in the Premier League table - though a point clear of the bottom three - while their opponents drop two places to 15th.
The two sides are on their travels when they return to action next Sunday; Forest head to Liverpool and Luton are away at Aston Villa.
Thank you for joining us today.
Until next time, goodbye!
